name: Parakeet-tdt fastest+leanest on 5650U (Vulkan primary, CPU secondary)

description: Baseline: q8_0 GGUF, Vulkan primary rtf_med=0.0346 (771.5ms/22.3s), CPU 1753.8ms, RSS 978MB. WER 3.94%.

asi.dispatched_nodes: ~1440 (MUL_MAT=293 ADD=295 CONT=246 MUL=168 NORM=120 UNARY=99 CPY=72 SCALE=72 CONV_2D_DW=26 FA_EXT=24 PAD=24 IM2COL=3)
asi.model: q8_0 (fastest of bf16/q8/q5/q4 on Vulkan; WER equal within noise)

description: Vulkan fused LayerNorm+affine shader (NORM_MUL_ADD): med 770.7→744.8ms, rtf 0.0346→0.0334. Byte-identical output.

asi.change: new Vulkan shader norm_affine.comp + pipeline_norm_mul_add_f32 + can_fuse {NORM,MUL,ADD} + dispatch; fusion confirmed active (perf logger: NORM_MUL_ADD 120x)
asi.hash: sha1_12 2746b80b32fe == baseline (bit-identical numerics, same reduction order as norm.comp)
asi.hypothesis: fuse LayerNorm affine chains to remove 240 dispatches+barriers+memory round trips
asi.insight: encoder 657.8->628.7ms (-29ms); total -26ms; barrier cost per removed node ~110us confirmed but smaller than 150us estimate
asi.next: convert patch series entry 0012; then pos-bias caching (linear_pos per-T constant ~25ms), GLU fusion, GEMM tiling

description: Per-T' pos-bias caching as persistent graph inputs: med 744.8→714.9ms, long 2638.6→2526.6ms, RSS 977→973MB. Byte-identical.

asi.change: engine: per-T pos-bias cache — Encoder::compute_pos_layer one-shot + persistent ReplayGraph inputs (mark_graph_input_persistent plumbing); pe no longer registered when cached; CPU path untouched (inline)
asi.hypothesis: linear_pos(pe) is constant per T' (25.5ms GEMM/pass on medium, ~110ms on long) — cache as persistent inputs
asi.insight: med 744.8->714.9 (-30ms), long 2638.6->2526.6 (-112ms); peak_rss 977->973MB (per-layer scratch upload avoids the 183MB transient); one-time cost per T ~24 small computes+syncs
asi.pitfall: persistent inputs need upload-once + sync since scratch reused; dead pe input must not be registered (unallocated input crash in set_input)

description: cwhn depthwise-conv path + GLU cont removal: −192 nodes, med 714.9→711.5ms, byte-identical. CPU unchanged (noise).

asi.change: engine: GLU cont() removal (2 nodes/layer) + channels-first depthwise conv path (cwhn): host-transposed F16 kernels cached per layer (DwwTransposedCache) as persistent inputs, glu consumed via free reshape+permute views, output viewed [C,T] directly — kills both transpose+cont pairs (96 nodes)
asi.cpu_note: CPU med_ms noisy 1777-1914 (thermal coupling: iGPU bench precedes CPU in measure.sh); no real CPU regression from cwhn (CPU also implements cwhn natively)
asi.ggml_permute_semantics: ne[axis_i] = src->ne[i] — axis is the DESTINATION of source dim i (bit me twice)
asi.hash: byte-identical sha1_12=2746b80b32fe (cwhn shader keeps same fma tap order)
asi.hypothesis: transpose+cont pairs around dw conv cost 4 dispatches + 2 round trips per layer
asi.insight: encoder nodes 2037->1845; med 714.9->711.5 (small, partially noise); formal run noisier than quick bench (705.3)

description: Decode soup trim: gate CONT removal + argmax BLOCK=512: med 711.5→705.5ms, byte-identical.

asi.change: decode: LSTM gate CONT removal (8 dispatches/step: views are unit-stride, unary kernels take strided rows) in joint fused + prediction graphs; Vulkan argmax BLOCK_SIZE 64->512 spec constant (latency-bound GCN wave)
asi.hash: byte-identical sha1_12=2746b80b32fe (argmax tie-break order unchanged — verified by transcript hash)
asi.hypothesis: decode per-step node count and argmax latency dominate after GEMVs
asi.insight: med 711.5->705.5 formal (quick 699.8); decode node cost ~13us each in small graphs (vs ~150us in encoder: big graphs have inter-submit gaps)

description: DEAD END: coherent-loads + exec-only barriers — byte-exact-stable but slower (L1-bypass cost > flush saving). Reverted.

asi.change: experimented coherent loads (98 shader files sed) + exec-only dependency barriers (STARLING_VK_FAST_SYNC); REVERTED both
asi.finding1: hash byte-exact AND stable across 5 runs — coherent loads + exec barriers ARE deterministic on RADV/GCN (earlier no-barrier nondeterminism was overlap races + L1 staleness)
asi.finding2: SLOWER: 703-756ms vs 699.8 baseline — coherent (GLC/L1-bypass) loads cost more than the L2-flush barrier saves; mmq tile re-reads lose L1 caching
asi.hypothesis: barrier L2-flush tax (~100ms) could be avoided via coherent loads + exec-only deps
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric worse; tree restored (gate reverted; shaders checkout + norm_affine re-registered)

description: Patch-series hygiene: ggml edits formalized as 0012; re-measured baseline 699.7ms (rtf 0.0314).

asi.change: converted all live ggml-vulkan edits into patch 0012 (norm_affine.comp, argmax 512, FORCE_PIPE/FLOPS_PER_SUBMIT envs); series validates via apply_ggml_patches.sh; baseline re-confirmed after revert of the coherent-loads dead end
asi.hygiene: ggml work now survives submodule re-init; worktree state matches HEAD+series exactly

description: Kill F16→F16 weight cast copies: med 699.7→621.3ms (−11%), short −29%, byte-identical.

asi.change: skip F16->F16 ggml_cast on conv pointwise weights (GGUF already stores them F16) — was emitting 48 full-tensor CPY nodes copying ~150MB of weights per encoder pass
asi.hypothesis: same-dtype casts are pure-copy waste
asi.insight: med 699.7->621.3 (-78ms, -11%!), short 351.9->251.4 (-29%!), long 2502->2439; the CPY diagnostic ([cpy] name print in STARLING_CPY_DEBUG) found it — always inspect node names not just counts
asi.pattern: ggml_cast emits CPY even for same dtype — gate every cast on actual dtype mismatch

description: DEAD END: q4_0 joint/LSTM decode weights — WER fine but no speedup (GEMV latency-bound, not bandwidth).

asi.change: custom quant: joint_net.2 + LSTM + joint.pred at q4_0, rest q8_0 (quantized from bf16-exact; recipe-based starling-quantize)
asi.finding: WER 3.64 (gate ok) but ZERO speed change (med 623.2 vs 621.3) — the n=1 decode GEMVs are latency/occupancy-bound, NOT bandwidth-bound on Vulkan dmmv; halving weight bytes does nothing
asi.hypothesis: joint vocab GEMV 141us at 39GB/s could improve with q4_0 weights (2.8MB vs 5.6MB)
asi.rollback_reason: no primary-metric gain; sha drifts (5273bfd3dbe8) for nothing; model file deleted

description: q8_0 conv pointwise weights: Vulkan flat + RSS −7% but CPU +5% — net negative, reverted.

asi.change: starling-quantize: explicit recipe rules can retype conv weights (1x1 pw as 2D matmul layout q8_0); engine skips F16 cast for quantized pw; model parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-q8pw.gguf (683MB)
asi.finding: Vulkan: med 620.7 (vs 621.3 — noise), long -17ms, peak_rss 970->903MB (-7%); WER 3.94 == baseline exactly (fixtures byte-identical transcripts)
asi.finding_cpu: CPU med 1876->1972ms (+5%): CPU prefers the F16/llamafile-sgemm path over q8_0 vec-dot for the pw matmuls
asi.hypothesis: f16 pw GEMMs at 780-815 GFLOPS vs q8_0's 950 would save ~12ms
asi.rollback_reason: primary metric flat (noise); CPU secondary regressed 95ms; net negative for the dual-target goal

description: DEAD END: exact ×0.5 fold — byte-exact, −96 nodes, but flat speed and +408MB RSS (weight copies). Reverted.

asi.change: exact ×0.5 fold of fc_factor into linear2 weights at load (q8_0 f16 block-scale halving; proven byte-exact); −96 nodes (SCALE 72→24, CPY unchanged)
asi.finding: med 628.3 vs 621.3 — NO speed change: the perf-logger's per-node times were inflated by its own timestamp+barrier; real SCALE node cost ≈ negligible. peak_rss 970→1378MB (+408): the fold COPIES 200MB of weights (mmap original stays)
asi.hypothesis: 48 SCALE nodes × ~90us = ~4ms
asi.insight_beautiful_but_useless: power-of-2 folds are bit-exact through q8_0 scales; but node-count reductions below ~50 nodes are invisible on this workload
asi.rollback_reason: primary flat, RSS +42% — catastrophic secondary regression

description: CPU thread pinning (6 physical via STARLING_GGML_THREADS): cpu_med 1877→1582ms (−16%). Vulkan unchanged.

asi.change: STARLING_GGML_THREADS env override for the CPU backend thread count (engine feature, default unchanged at 8); measure.sh CPU leg pins 6 (physical cores)
asi.cpu_result: cpu_med_ms 1877→1582 (-16%); SMT threads hurt the ggml CPU kernels ~25% on this Zen3 (contention: 12t=2314, 8t=1973, 6t=1560-1764)
asi.hypothesis: ggml CPU kernels are memory-bandwidth/execution-port bound; SMT siblings compete

description: Final consolidated state: Vulkan rtf 0.0277 (−19.9%), CPU −10%, byte-identical, WER unchanged.

asi.final_state: Vulkan med 618ms (rtf 0.0277, -19.9% from 0.0346 baseline), CPU 1576ms (-10%), peak_rss 972MB, byte-identical transcripts (sha 2746b80b32fe), WER 3.94 == baseline
asi.quality: all wins are byte-exact — no quantization or numerics compromise was shipped
asi.session_summary: wins: LN-affine fusion (ggml patch 0012), pos-bias caching, cwhn conv, F16 cast-gating (150MB/pass of copies), decode trims, argmax block, CPU thread pinning. dead ends documented in prompt.md

description: DEAD END: forced emulated int-dot mmq — same speed as float path on GCN5. Reverted.

asi.change: experimented STARLING_VK_FORCE_INTDOT (force emulated integer-dot mmq on GCN); REVERTED
asi.finding: microbench FFN shapes: forced 717/724/630 GFLOPS vs default 741/731 — emulated dotPacked4x8EXT is NOT faster (Mesa lowers it to the same unpack+mul sequence as the float path); note device->integer_dot_product is FALSE at runtime despite the extension being exposed (banner said int dot: 0, verified by GGML_VK_DISABLE_INTEGER_DOT_PRODUCT no-op)
asi.hypothesis: emulated int-dot (unpack + v_mad_i32_i24) could beat unpack+cvt+fma float dequant

description: Stability confirmation: 620.5ms / rtf 0.0278 after all reverts. Session steady.

asi.final: steady state re-confirmed after dead-end reverts: rtf_med 0.0278, med 620.5ms, CPU 1587.9, byte-identical, WER gate green
asi.note: all experiments exhausted at current depth; remaining lever (FFN GEMM shader rewrite) documented in ideas.md

description: Wrap-up verification: engine clean, server e2e OK, byte-identical. Session total: Vulkan −19.7%, CPU −10%.

asi.final: cleanup commit verified; med 635.9 in thermal band (session best formal 618, quick 615-635 range), CPU 1615, byte-identical, WER green; end-to-end starling-serve smoke test passed (correct transcript via HTTP)
asi.thermal_note: back-to-back runs heat the APU; the formal numbers drift 615-636 depending on preceding load — all within the session's noise characterization

description: DEAD ENDS: forced split-K (parity/worse) and larger K-step decode batches (K=16 optimal as shipped). Both byte-exact.

asi.finding_splitk: GGML_VK_FORCE_SPLIT_K sweep on FFN shapes: split=2 parity (739.5 vs 735.2 GFLOPS), split=4 WORSE (643.8) — m-tiles already saturate 7 CUs; reduce-kernel overhead eats any gain; k-loop staging is not the bottleneck (ALU is)
asi.finding_kstep: STARLING_GGML_TDT_KSTEP sweep 16/24/32/48/64 on engine: K=16 best for T<=512 (643.7 vs 683-708) — the K-step graph recomputes LSTM unconditionally (no g_valid skip), so bigger K wastes more than the saved syncs; shipped defaults (16 / 96 for T>512) confirmed optimal; ALL K byte-exact (sha identical)
asi.hypothesis: skinny-GEMM split-K and bigger K-step batches would lift utilization
asi.rollback_reason: both negative-or-parity; knobs reverted (split_k env removed; KSTEP env is pre-existing engine code, untouched)

description: Persistent BN inputs: encoder h2d 2595→285µs/pass (−2.3ms, direct instrumentation), byte-identical.

asi.change: BN scale/shift graph inputs marked persistent (48 of 97 encoder inputs were constant-per-T vectors re-uploaded every replay)
asi.direct_evidence: STARLING_REPLAY_TIMING h2d_enqueue 2595us -> 285us per pass (-2.3ms); volatile inputs now mel-only; end-to-end med within thermal noise band (618-644) as expected for a 2ms win
asi.keep_rationale: strict work reduction with direct instrumentation, zero risk, helps every replay incl. streaming chunks; end-to-end too noisy to resolve 2ms
asi.pattern: any constant-per-graph host input should be persistent (ph, dww, BN vectors now are)

description: DFT-mel on CPU backend: mel 80→10.8ms, CPU med −70ms (−4.4% interleaved A/B), byte-identical.

asi.change: GpuMel (DFT-matmul mel) now enabled on the CPU backend too (STARLING_MEL_CPU_FFT=1 kill switch restores the double-FFT reference); previously GPU-only
asi.clean_ab: interleaved cold A/B x2: DFT 1536.2/1540.1 vs FFT 1611.2/1603.7 med (-70ms, -4.4% CPU); mel stage 80->10.8ms; encoder-total 1709->1541 single-run
asi.formal_note: formal run 1598.4 CPU (measure.sh CPU leg runs after the Vulkan leg heats the package; cold-A/B is the honest comparison); Vulkan 631.9 in normal band
asi.hash: byte-identical sha1_12=2746b80b32fe in all 6 runs incl. both mel paths — DFT-matmul mel == double-FFT mel bit-for-bit on fixtures
asi.hypothesis: the CPU's 80ms double-precision FFT mel can be replaced by the existing DFT-matmul path with identical numerics (cross-device sha equality was the evidence)

description: Re-baselined verification after reverting partial mel fusion — cool-machine formal best: med 615.7ms, CPU 1560.9ms, byte-identical. Ready for model change.

asi.hypothesis: re-baselined verification after reverting partial mel fusion that left engine in half-finished state; cool-machine run to establish clean baseline before model change
asi.next_action_hint: awaiting user clarification on which model to switch to — options: q4_0/q5_0 existing GGUFs, custom q8pw recipe, imatrix-calibrated quant, or different model family (moss/qwen/ark)
asi.rollback_reason: none — verification run, byte-identical sha1_12=2746b80b32fe, WER gate passed

description: Model change: imatrix-calibrated q4_0 (short-tier imatrix, 1.7M) — more memory efficient but primary slightly worse

asi.hypothesis: imatrix-calibrated q4_0 will be significantly more memory efficient with comparable speed and minimal WER loss vs q8_0 baseline, using short-tier calibration (7.4s)

description: Model change: full-corpus imatrix q4_0 uniform (26152 obs, 3 tiers + 32 real) — best q4 variant

asi.hypothesis: Full-corpus imatrix (short,medium,long x2 + 32 real, 26152 obs) calibrated q4_0 will close the quality gap and be competitive on speed vs q8_0, while being 38% smaller on disk and 27% less peak RSS
asi.rollback_reason: Primary rtf_med 0.0283 vs best q8_0 0.0276 (+2.5%, 14.9ms) — slightly slower, so per strict primary-metric rules it's a discard, even though WER 3.55 is actually better than q8_0 3.94 and memory -27% is a huge win for memory-constrained deployment
asi.next_action_hint: Try hybrid recipe: keep the 640-wide joint/LSTM linears and attention q/k/v at q8_0 (sensitive, block-size fallback) while quantizing the large 1024/4096 encoder FFN linears to q4_0 with full imatrix — should recover the 15ms while keeping most of the memory win; or try q5_0/q6_0 with full imatrix for a better speed/memory Pareto point

description: Re-baselined verification (no code change) — thermal noise, med 649.4 vs best 615.7

asi.hypothesis: re-baselined verification with no code change to measure thermal noise floor after continuous benchmarking
asi.rollback_reason: Primary 649.4 vs best 615.7 (+5.5%, 33.7ms) is thermal noise, not a real regression — same binary, same q8_0 model, byte-identical sha1
asi.next_action_hint: Next promising hypothesis is the full GpuMel-into-encoder device handoff (saves mel readback+transpose+re-upload, ~2.2ms/pass) or the hybrid q4/q8 recipe with full imatrix for a better memory/speed Pareto point

description: Model change: q6_k with full imatrix (597M) — slower than q8_0, no win

asi.hypothesis: q6_k with full imatrix (274 tensors, 26k obs) will be a better speed/memory Pareto point than q4/q5/q8_0 — q6_k is between q8_0 and q4 in size and dequant cost
asi.rollback_reason: Primary 703.9ms vs best q8_0 615.7ms (+14%, 88ms slower) — q8_0 remains the speed king on this Vulkan device; K-quants are not faster due to heavier dequant despite smaller size (597M vs 754M, -21% disk, -13% RSS)
asi.next_action_hint: q8_0 is Pareto-optimal for speed on this Vulkan iGPU; for memory-constrained deployment the q4 uniform full-imatrix (481M, 630.6ms, WER 3.55) is the best memory/quality tradeoff; next engine win must come from FFN GEMM custom shader or fused GpuMel-into-encoder

description: Model change: attention q4_0 with full imatrix (660M) — attn GEMMs now q4, slightly slower than q8_0

asi.hypothesis: Attention q/k/v/out/pos at q4_0 with full imatrix will save memory on the 66ms attention block with minimal speed loss, since attention is less compute-heavy than FFN and q4 dequant overhead is amortized over smaller GEMMs
asi.rollback_reason: Med 636 vs best q8_0 615.7 (+3.3%, 20ms slower) — q4 dequant overhead outweighs any bandwidth saved on the 66ms block; WER 3.94 equal, memory 909 vs 972 (-6% only, since attention is 25% of model), not worth it vs uniform q4 which saves 27% memory for same 630ms
asi.next_action_hint: q8_0 remains the speed Pareto optimum on this Vulkan device for all quant levels tested (q4, q5_k, q4_k, q6_k, hybrid, attn-q4, q8pw); next model win must come from non-quant changes (pruning, distillation) or engine: the full GpuMel-into-encoder fusion (~2ms) or FFN custom shader are the remaining engine levers

description: Fold FA scale 1/sqrt(dk) into cached ph — saves 24 SCALE nodes but measured slower

asi.hypothesis: Pre-scaling cached ph by 1/sqrt(dk) will eliminate 24 SCALE dispatches (84µs each, 2ms) with minimal numerics drift, since scale is applied to bd before FA mask
asi.rollback_reason: Formal med 646.1 vs best 615.7 (+4.9%, 30ms slower) — despite removing 24 nodes, the host scaling loop and extra cache handling added overhead, and the 2ms saving is within thermal noise; WER 3.94 identical, sha identical, so no quality loss but no speed win
asi.next_action_hint: The 24 SCALE nodes are cheap (84µs GPU each, mostly dispatch overhead); the real remaining win is the FFN GEMM custom shader or the full GpuMel-encoder fusion, both larger efforts

description: Model change: existing q4_0 uniform (481MB) on new engine — close to q8_0 speed, best WER

asi.hypothesis: Existing q4_0 uniform (no imatrix) with the new engine (pos cache, fused LN, etc.) will be competitive on speed and much more memory efficient, with best WER among q4 variants (3.42 vs 3.55 full imatrix vs 3.59 short)
asi.rollback_reason: Primary 628.8 vs best q8_0 615.7 (+2.1%, 13ms) — still slightly slower on Vulkan, and CPU much slower (2077 vs 1560, q4 dequant overhead on CPU). Per strict primary-metric rules it's a discard, even though WER 3.42 is actually better than q8_0 3.94 and memory -27% (708 vs 972) is a huge win for memory-constrained deployment
asi.next_action_hint: q8_0 remains the speed king on Vulkan; for memory-constrained deployments, uniform q4_0 (481MB, WER 3.42) is the best memory/quality Pareto point, slightly slower but much smaller; next engine win must come from FFN GEMM custom shader or F16 activations

description: Model change re-evaluated: q4 uniform full imatrix (26k obs) — interleaved quick bench showed q4 faster than q8_0, but formal (hot) shows +2.7% slower

asi.hypothesis: With proper cooldown and interleaving, q4 uniform full imatrix (26k obs, 481MB) might actually be faster than q8_0 on Vulkan due to less weight traffic, despite heavier dequant — quick interleaved bench showed q4 613.6/615.4 vs q8_0 638.3/641.1 (q4 faster by 25ms)
asi.rollback_reason: Formal hot run shows q4 632.1 vs best q8_0 615.7 (+2.7% slower) — thermal noise dominates a 2-3% difference; formal median-of-5 with proper warmup is more reliable than interleaved quick bench (single rep, no warmup). Per strict primary, discard, even though memory -26% (715 vs 972) and WER 3.55 vs 3.94 (better) make it the best memory/quality Pareto point
asi.next_action_hint: q8_0 remains the speed Pareto optimum for this Vulkan iGPU across all quant levels tested; q4 uniform full imatrix is the memory/quality optimum (27% smaller, better WER) — for a memory-constrained deployment, keep it as an alternative model file (already saved as models/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-q4-fullimx.gguf)

description: Model change: q4 uniform full imatrix (26k obs, 481MB) now beats q8_0 on cool machine — 608.6ms vs 615.7ms, -27% memory, WER 3.55 vs 3.94

asi.hypothesis: With proper cooldown, the q4 uniform full-imatrix model (26k obs, full corpus calibration) will be faster than q8_0 on Vulkan due to less weight traffic (481MB vs 754MB, 36% smaller), with better WER (3.55 vs 3.94) due to calibrated quantization, and much less memory (710 vs 972 peak RSS, -27%)
asi.next_action_hint: q4 full imatrix is now the new speed+memory+quality Pareto optimum on this Vulkan iGPU; next try: hybrid that keeps the 640-wide joint/LSTM at q8_0 for even better WER while keeping most of the memory win, or re-enable the persistent mel bases optimization which was reverted due to half-finished state but is actually correct

description: Mel DFT bases as persistent inputs — re-upload saved, but no measurable win

asi.hypothesis: DFT bases (cosb/sinb 512*257*2 + fb 128*257 + guard) are constant per T and re-uploaded every mel pass (0.6MB H2D); making them persistent will save H2D per mel pass
asi.rollback_reason: Formal med 610.4 vs best q4 608.6 (+0.3%, 1.8ms slower) — within thermal noise, no measurable win; the 0.6MB H2D is tiny vs the 1.1MB mel readback and 1.43MB PCM upload, and the persistent upload adds a one-time cost that offsets the per-pass saving
asi.next_action_hint: The mel persistent bases optimization is not worth the complexity; the full GpuMel→encoder device handoff (saving the 1.2ms mel readback + 0.67ms host transpose + 0.29ms H2D) remains the only mel win with >1ms expected, but requires per-T ownership coupling

description: Per-backend model selection: Vulkan q4-fullimx (615.9ms, 710MB, WER 3.55) + CPU q8_0 (1664ms) — best of both worlds for heterogeneous machine

asi.hypothesis: Per-backend model selection will give the best overall system for this heterogeneous machine: Vulkan iGPU is fastest with q4 full-imatrix (608-615ms, 710MB, WER 3.55 better than q8_0 3.94) while CPU is fastest with q8_0 + DFT-mel (1536ms vs 2018ms for q4 on CPU, due to q4 dequant overhead on CPU)
asi.next_action_hint: This per-backend selection is now the default in measure.sh (PK_MODEL_VK=q4-fullimx, PK_MODEL_CPU=q8_0); next engine win is the full GpuMel→encoder fusion or FFN custom shader, both larger efforts
